scope: Six distinct exact-law targets and interfaces; no new scientific verification.

receivers.input_contract: Known starting labels, positive epochs/rates, current-block independent routing and common competitor class.
receivers.result: Scoped canonical history identification, with distinct two-copy, three-copy and later expansion contracts.
receivers.limit: Not unrestricted biological encoding, continuous migration or simultaneous-event factorization.

receivers.input_contract: Full-column-rank routing and legal pair/triple short-time events after known-prefix inversion.
receivers.result: Classical whitening/cubic algebra recovers routing and rates, including ties.
receivers.limit: Three copies not proved minimal; mathematical inverse not physical intervention.

receivers.input_contract: Reachable canonical finite-epoch class, legal nested forests and complete balanced panel.
receivers.result: Later reviewed coherent hidden-name classification and effective finite bound.
receivers.limit: Local independent permutations alone insufficient; arbitrary computable-real comparison and practical bounds separate.

receivers.input_contract: Known stationary clock-JC channel, shared genealogy at a locus and specified panel.
receivers.result: Reviewed polynomial three-tip complete-law cutoff; global bridge uses its full balanced panel.
receivers.limit: Not finite-locus confidence, unknown clock, recombination or lower/minimal bound.

receivers.input_contract: Admitted COMMON source and row-labelled fixed joint forcing laws across allocations.
receivers.result: Target-adaptive finite legal observations determine each entire weighted-tree response row.
receivers.limit: Not graph recovery, cross-row joint counterfactual law, implemented search or finite-I theorem.

receivers.input_contract: Observed selected no-merger event, positive measured denominator and feasible correlated seed posterior at interior cut.
receivers.result: Frozen right-germ equality determines occupancy support.
receivers.limit: Not full hidden posterior, rates/graph identification or physical continuation past boundary.
